codebase.title: MRSimulator — solid-state NMR spectral simulation

agent_authored.description: MRSimulator is a Python/Cython/C package for rapid frequency-domain simulation of one- and two-dimensional solid-state NMR spectra. It models spin systems, shielding and quadrupolar interactions, pulse methods, orientation sampling, and signal processing for chemical and materials-science workflows.

modules.title: Solid-state NMR spin-system and spectrum simulation
modules.expensive_path: Compiled spectrum evaluation: transition enumeration, tensor-frequency contributions, orientation/sampling integration, C-level interpolation and histogram accumulation over spin systems and spectral dimensions.
modules.rationale: The simulator, method definitions, spin-system model, transitions, tensor utilities, signal processing and C kernels form one tightly coupled public package. The owned source is about 29.7k lines, below the repository's task-sizing threshold, and the official tests exercise the same end-to-end spectral path. A single module keeps the physical observable (the simulated spectrum) intact instead of separating data structures from the kernel they feed.
excluded: docs/ and documentation-only doctest examples that require external ssnmr.org downloads are not packaged as implementation paths.
examples_source/ and fitting_source/ are retained as upstream examples but are not owned implementation paths; their data-heavy or external-tool workflows are outside the first task.
pyplot/ and plotting-only helpers are not an acceleration target; plotting remains available through the package but is not a graded numerical path.
hazards: The build requires a C compiler, Cython, NumPy headers, OpenBLAS and FFTW; missing headers must fail image probes rather than being installed at run time.
Orientation averaging and BLAS reductions can differ by a few ulps across legitimate builds, so tolerances must be calibrated from nominal/variant and any declared altbuild runs.
Three fitting documentation examples require external ssnmr.org data and are not reproducible from the pinned checkout alone.
Several tests use doctest and CSDM objects; checks must grade physical spectral arrays or scalar observables, not plotting bytes or storage order.
